new_statements.rule_in_words: Pangseng, like every Mumuye lect Shimizu recorded, has three contrastive level tones (High, Mid, Low) plus a High-Low falling contour (and a Low-High rise in some items); the work says nothing about word stress or accent (full-text queries 'stress', 'accent', 'pitch', 'intonation' return zero hits in the volume).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonally, the HL fall is recorded 'in many of the dialects' and its Proto-Mumuye status is left open; a LH rise occurs in HE/SHE and some other items (n.23, p.68).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about lexical tone on syllables across the 14 Mumuye lects of a comparative wordlist study (citation forms); it is group-wide, not a Pangseng-specific phonology, and was read via Google Books snippets plus full-text index, not page images.
new_statements.identity_note: Shimizu 1979 treats 'Pangseng' as one of 14 Mumuye lects in his comparative wordlist study and remarks (p.52) that Rang and Pangseng 'stand on their own linguistically'; his tone statement (p.27) is made for 'all the dialects studied', i.e. it covers Pangseng but is not Pangseng-specific. Ethnologue/Blench list Pangseng varieties Pangseng, Komo, Jega (spoken at Jinlari on the Zing-Lankaviri road). The fuller Mumuye grammar (Shimizu 1983) describes the Zing dialect = nucl1240, not Pangseng.
